cases.emailBody:
Hello,

We are reviewing your invoice and have a few points to query before we can post it.

Please confirm whether this invoice has been submitted to us before, as it appears to match an earlier posted invoice.

Please confirm the unit prices for the lines below, as they differ from the order and from your recent invoices.

{TABLE}

Kind regards

findings.explanation: This line is invoiced for 10 but only 8 has been received and not yet invoiced, leaving 2 not received, worth GBP 212.00. The invoice is ahead of delivery, so hold it until the goods arrive.

The invoice unit cost is GBP 106.00 against GBP 100.00 on the order, a difference of 6%, or GBP 60.00, which is above the 2% tolerance. This is likely an unagreed price rise or a wrong price list, so ask the vendor to confirm the price.

The invoice unit cost of GBP 106.00 is 6% above the GBP 100.00 on the latest posted invoice line, compared across 1 posted invoice line, a difference of GBP 60.00. This supports the order price finding, so ask the vendor to confirm the price.
This freight charge of GBP 150.00 has no purchase order or receipt behind it. Assigning it as an item charge lets the cost reach the item cost.

A quantity of 1 on the inbound freight item charge is not assigned to receipt lines, worth GBP 75.00. The invoice cannot be posted until the charge is fully assigned, so assign it to the receipt lines.

A posted invoice from this vendor has a vendor invoice number that matches this one once spaces and symbols are removed, and the same amount of GBP 1,535.00. This may be the same invoice entered twice, so query it before posting.
